goal: Preserve independently authorized external feature transport attempts in the selected private stores without building MFM or personality, performing live inference, inventing usage or replaying one exchange as multiple attempts.

Bind each supplied external task to the registered frozen run, question, phase history, independently authorized context, exact compiled provider body, token receipt and enrolled observer. Verify actual original-memory wire semantics with the frozen compiler; leave native feature-packet semantics to a separately qualified verifier. Compare the caller's current source authorization marker, bind it to the exact private task digest, record a single-use dispatch authorization under an atomic per-arm/phase attempt budget, and recheck before transfer. Verify actual supplied observer signatures and request/response bytes, parse known usage only from complete response bytes, preserve partial or unavailable material without estimates, and store observed attempts separately from inference history. authority: Procedure trace only. The ledger records independently supplied grants and signed first-party observations; it grants no disclosure authority, certifies no provider internals or transport quality, supplies no learned judgment, and establishes no FloRA behavior advantage or customer traction.

The physical selected-backend test is prepared for CI and has not yet qualified the new ledger. No live API response, real tokenizer, provider bill or model prediction was used.
failure_or_lesson: A source-only authorization marker is identical for retries with equal wire bytes and unchanged grants. Without the exact private task digest, one signed observation could be replayed into multiple denominator rows. Dispatch permission is not dispatch completion. Separate local capture can preserve already observed consumed usage after external or evaluation withdrawal, while private audit still requires current ancestor authority.
